findings.finding: node-e-fs destructive-call poison only detects fs.rmSync/fs.unlinkSync/fs.rmdirSync member calls, so an aliased/destructured destructive fs call can still be auto-approved when co-present with fs.writeFileSync.
findings.evidence: matchNodeEFs first checks /fs\.(rmSync|unlinkSync|rmdirSync)\b/ then approves on /fs\.(writeFileSync|appendFileSync|mkdirSync)\b/. A command shaped as node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const {rmSync}=require('fs'); fs.writeFileSync('out.js','x'); rmSync(targetVar)" returns {scope:"node-e-fs",...}. This is the same mixed write+destructive variable-delete class; extractDeleteTargets still has no literal target to catch.
findings.remediation: Make node -e approval all-or-nothing for destructive fs calls including destructured/aliased imports or require-bound calls, or parse the node -e body conservatively and reject any rmSync/unlinkSync/rmdirSync identifier reachable from fs before granting node-e-fs.
